holidays.name: World Ceviche Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the zesty Latin American dish of raw fish 'cooked' in citrus juice. Seafood lovers celebrate by marinating, squeezing limes, and arguing about whose abuela makes it best.
holidays.origin: Peru declared ceviche a national heritage dish and has celebrated it on June 28 officially, but many food calendars and fans also observe World Ceviche Day on May 8 to spotlight the dish's global popularity.
holidays.funFact: The acid in lime juice doesn't truly cook the fish; it denatures the proteins, making the flesh turn opaque and firm, much like heat does.

holidays.name: No Socks Day
holidays.description: A day to liberate your feet from their cotton prisons. Participants go sockless in shoes, sandals, or bare feet and enjoy the breezy freedom, laundry-pile reduction, and mild risk of blisters.
holidays.origin: No Socks Day is an unofficial, tongue-in-cheek observance that spread through social media and quirky holiday calendars, celebrated on May 8 as spring warms up and sandal season begins.
holidays.funFact: Socks are famously the single most common item that vanishes in laundry, so skipping them means one fewer lonely sock widowed in the dryer.

holidays.name: World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day
holidays.description: A global observance honoring the humanitarian work of volunteers who provide disaster relief, blood donation, and emergency aid across nearly every country on Earth.
holidays.origin: Observed on May 8, the birthday of Henry Dunant, the Swiss founder of the Red Cross, who was also the first recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
holidays.funFact: The Red Cross emblem is the Swiss flag with colors reversed, a tribute to Dunant's home country.

holidays.name: World Thalassaemia Day
holidays.description: An awareness day highlighting the inherited blood disorder thalassaemia, encouraging screening, better treatment access, and support for patients and families worldwide.
holidays.origin: Established by the Thalassaemia International Federation in 1994 and held on May 8 in memory of Panos Englezos, the federation's founder's son who died of the disease.
holidays.funFact: The name comes from the Greek 'thalassa' meaning sea, because the disease was first noticed in people around the Mediterranean.

holidays.name: VE Day (Victory in Europe Day)
holidays.description: A day marking the end of World War II in Europe, celebrated with parades, street parties, and moments of remembrance. In some places it blends solemn tribute with tea, bunting, and vintage-style swing dancing.
holidays.origin: On May 8, 1945, Germany's unconditional surrender took effect, sparking enormous celebrations in London, Paris, and elsewhere.
holidays.funFact: On VE Day, a young Princess Elizabeth and Princess Margaret slipped out of Buckingham Palace incognito to join the crowds celebrating in the streets.
